steps.text: Combine half-and-half, sugar, cream, vanilla, and salt in the freezer container of an ice cream maker.
Freeze according to the manufacturer’s instructions, about 20 minutes.
Transfer to an airtight container and freeze until firm, about 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Ice Cream
raw_recipe.description: This easy homemade ice cream is made with just cream, sugar, and vanilla for an old-fashioned vanilla ice cream that’s sure to be a summer hit!
raw_recipe.name: Homemade Ice Cream

recipeInstructions.text: Combine half-and-half, sugar, cream, vanilla, and salt in the freezer container of an ice cream maker.

Transfer to an airtight container and freeze until firm, about 4 hours.

review.reviewBody: Ok this recipe was so easy and for all of you who loved it try this: I added 1/4 cup of Carnation Coffee-Mate French Vanilla creamer this added a wonderfull flavor and everyone wanted to know what I did to make it taste so rich. worked great will keep this recipe

I have made this recipe numerous times with numerous alterations and have finally find the one that works for me. I decrease the extract (personal preference). I heat the half-n-half/cream and sugar on the stove until the sugar is dissolved the night before I want to make the ice cream. I chill the mixture all night. I put the ice cream in my ice cream maker for about 25 min. Put it in the freezer for about 2 hours. Take it out and let it soften a little and serve. It was wonderful!! I make it way to often and my chocaholic son never seems to mind that it is vanilla!

I chose to make this recipe my first try at vanilla ice cream due to no cooking required and no raw eggs in it. I used homemade vanilla (from this website), so the ice cream had little specks of vanilla bean in it, and was nice and creamy. The instructions say to mix the ingredients together IN the freezer container of the ice cream maker; don't do that if you have the kind of ice cream maker with the already-frozen canister! Mix them in a bowl and then add to the ice cream maker! Oh, I also scaled it down to 8 servings for my 1.5qt ice cream maker; it didn't make a lot; I think 16 servings would be about right for a full recipe. Thanks for the recipe, Jackie!

I made this as written and then did a second time with some adaptations with great results. First, I scaled in half for my 2 quart counter top ice cream maker. To get a better texture, I reduced the half and half to 3 cups and increased the heavy cream to 1-1/2 cups. To make sure you don't end up with a grainy texture, use a hand mixer to combine the half and half with the sugar for just a couple of minutes and then stir in the remaining ingredients. This is a soft serve ice cream, even straight from the freezer. We loved it!

Based on feedback I changed this to use a 2:1 ratio of heavy cream to half-n-half because some other recipes turned out a bit icy and I was looking for creamier. I also halved the recipe because my ice cream maker isn't that big and added two egg yolks to help emulsify. I mixed the ingredients together in the mixer for a minute or so prior to putting in the ice cream maker because my maker does not mix. As it was mixing, the cream started to whip up slightly so it had a bit of air in it. After about 10 minutes of mixing in the machine I added 3/4 cup of mini chocolate chips and some chopped walnuts (optional). As it came out of the ice cream maker I thought it was a failure because it was very light and tasted somewhat like whipped cream. But after being in the freezer for 3 hours it thickened considerably and was dense, creamy and amazing.

The only change I made was to stir about 1/3 cup hot water with sugar to melt before mixing everything else together. Homemade, churned ice cream which does not include simmering a custard first, is a light, crystally, semi-soft ice cream, similar to soft-serve you buy at Dairy Queen. Homemade ice cream must "ripen" or itnis super soft and melts almost immediately. Leave it in the container, pour out any water, pack with more ice and rock salt, and wrap the entiee freezer with a heavy beach towel. Let ripen as long as you like to "harden" 1-3 hours, ensuring ice is holding. Storebought ice cream has chemicals and additives that give it that "creamy" texture; homemade has none of that - so much better!!!!

This recipe is great -- maybe a tad too sweet, but that's probably just my personal taste. I'll probably reduce sugar to 1 cup next time. I used all half-and-half rather than part heavy cream. Also, it's completely possible to make this without an ice cream maker! Put the mixture into tupperware and freeze. Every 30-minutes to an hour, pour it into a blender and blend until smooth. Depending on the size of your blender you may need to process in two or three batches, because this recipe is huge. After a few hours it will blend to the consistency of a very thick milkshake -- at that point, just let it freeze untouched for a few more hours, and you'll have ice cream! The more often you blended it, the creamier it will be. It's more time-consuming than using an ice cream machine, but it also makes the final product all the more rewarding! And it's so cheap to make compared to store-bought. I can't wait to make again with different add-ins -- bits of candy bars, caramel syrup, peppermint extract and chocolate chips!

I read a ton of recipes and all the reviews before settling on this one. I mixed 3/4 cup brown sugar with 4 tsps strong coffee over heat until the sugar dissolved then I removed from heat and stirred in 3 cups heavy whipping cream, 1.5 cups of half and half, and a pinch of salt. I chilled this for two hours before processing in the ice cream maker. It is scaled down for a 2qt ice cream maker. Loved the creamy, rich, buttery, coffee soft serve I ended up with. We ate it immediately. Thanks for the guidance for my first go at ice cream!

We had company over this evening and I picked this recipe for dessert. I made it almost exactly according to the recipe (I didn't have half-and-half so I made my own with whole milk and cream). I dissolved the sugar in a bit of hot water. I also added 1/4 tsp each of almond and rum extract as a previous reviewer suggested, to bring out the vanilla flavor. I forgot the salt. 

The results were absolutely fantastic! Possibly the best ice cream I've ever made. We all got seconds. And were horrified at the end of the evening to discover we'd accidentally eaten the ENTIRE batch of ice cream. Yes, 32 servings between the 6 of us. It was pretty awful--but it sure was tasty!

Do I recommend this recipe? Only if you want the most incredibly delicious and completely irresistible vanilla ice cream you've ever tasted. On a diet? You should probably cheat on something else.

Delicious! I didn’t have half and half, but I had whole milk and heavy cream, so I did 3 cups of whole milk, 1.5 cups heavy cream, 3/4 cup sugar, 2 teaspoons vanilla, and 1/2 pinch of salt (the recipe was scaled to 16 servings). Can’t wait to try this again with strawberries, blackberries, or peach purée!
Excellent. I halved the recipe for our ice cream maker and also dissolved the sugar on the stove with the half/half. Would be an easy recipe to modify with other flavors.
Very easy to make, we usually enjoy it with some simple rainbow sprinkles, fresh berries and chocolate sauce
Made as written, all kids enjoyed it with root beer. Not creamy if that is what you are looking for.
This is a great recipe! It turned out perfect!
Easy and delicious! I adjusted the serving size to 12 and also dissolved the sugar in the cream prior to mixing

This is our favorite ice cream! My only change is I take part of the half and half and add the sugar to it. Heat it in the microwave for a couple of minutes to totally dissolve the sugar. I add everything back into the freezer and process. So yummy!!
Took a chance and tried for first time at church social. Likes the “fluffiness” and “lightness”. Not too sweet and oh so easy.
